picks.title: Google Play Books' AI 'Book Insights' has launched
picks.excerpt: Google Play Books' AI-driven Book Insights has launched for thousands of select English titles. Google did not say if or when the tool will expand to non-English books.
picks.rationale: A live AI layer now sits on top of Play Books catalog pages, so publishers and indie authors have a new surface — and a new metadata dependency — to manage from today.

picks.title: Spotify adds more AI-powered discovery tools for audiobooks
picks.excerpt: New features let listeners auto-generate audiobook playlists from a prompt, ask natural-language questions about a book's contents, and track titles in a series.
picks.rationale: Prompt-generated playlists and in-book Q&A move audiobook discovery off keywords, which changes how series metadata and descriptions should be written right now.

picks.title: Warhammer 40,000 audiobook includes AI-training warning read out by the narrator
picks.excerpt: Games Workshop now has narrators read an anti-AI-training warning aloud at the top of Warhammer 40,000 audiobooks — a new front-matter convention for protecting publisher IP in audio.
picks.rationale: A spoken rights notice baked into the audio itself is a copyable production convention any audiobook publisher can adopt in the next session.

picks.title: Can AI replace your editor?
picks.excerpt: Michael La Ronn and Sacha Black answer member questions on where AI editing actually helps and where it fails, plus IngramSpark's return and series cover consistency.
picks.rationale: Draws the concrete line between the editing passes AI can carry and the ones it wrecks, plus series cover consistency — direct workbench guidance for authors and editors.

picks.title: Is it legal to train AI models on copyrighted books? It's complicated
picks.excerpt: Most published authors have, without their knowledge or consent, contributed to the AI tools that threaten their livelihoods. A plain-language guide to where the law actually stands.
picks.rationale: A plain-language map of where training-data law actually stands, which is what authors and agents need before signing or contesting an AI clause.
